title: About Justin Morrie Sacdalan
description: Meet Justin Morrie Sacdalan: Computer Science student, developer and digital creative at De La Salle University.

hero.eyebrow: A LITTLE ABOUT ME / JUSTIN MORRIE SACDALAN
hero.headline: Keep on keeping on
hero.accent: Until it's done, and done right.
hero.lede: Cheers! I'm Justin, a Computer Science student at De La Salle University in the Philippines. I like making things—and figuring out how to make them better while having fun.
hero.caption: web · software · digital media

sections.label: MORE ABOUT ME
sections.heading: My AGENT.md
sections.body:
If I had to write a quick guide to working with me, it would start with this: I don't take things at face value. Whether it's a dataset, a bug, or one of the many app ideas living rent-free in my head, I like to study it first, which is why most of my time goes into planning and setting things up. Give me a clear goal and a deadline, and it'll get done. Just know that I'll probably keep nitpicking the details until it actually feels right (perfectionism is both my strength and my biggest time sink).

Outside of coding, I'm into a lot of things, honestly. I build mechanical keyboards and Magic: The Gathering decks, practice my coffee-making (someday I'd love to run my own café), and window-shop PCs and laptops I definitely can't afford yet. I also play more gacha games than I'd like to admit, grind through Warframe and Monster Hunter, and binge manga and manhwa before chasing down the novels they came from.

Most of these interests sneak into my work one way or another. A few of my projects hide small references to the games and stories I love, so if you catch one, it'll probably make my day. If not, that's totally fine too (my tastes are kinda niche).

sections.label: ABOUT MY PROJECTS
sections.heading: Well of Ideas.
sections.body:
Ever since I was a child, I was drawn to the space between technology and digital creativity. A web application, an interface, a video, or an unfamiliar idea: I enjoy turning the initial concept into something people can use or enjoy.

My background is in web and software development, with hands-on work across React, Next.js, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python and Kotlin. I care as much about how an interface feels as how it works behind the scenes.

That curiosity has led to projects like [Gastos.io](/work/gastos-io), a personal expense tracker, and [Pocket Gains](/work/pocket-gains), a game-inspired workout companion. Each project is another chance to learn something new and refine the details.

sections.label: MORE THAN CODE
sections.heading: Building for people.
sections.body:
I’m part of **The LaSallian’s Web team**, contributing to website development and the digital publishing work of DLSU’s student publication. Working alongside an editorial team has given me a greater appreciation for clarity, accessibility and the people behind what appears on screen.

Beyond code, I explore graphic design, video editing and short-form content. I manage social media content independently; one TikTok channel has accumulated approximately 1.9 million views and 11,100 likes. Seeing an idea connect with an audience is just as rewarding as seeing software come together.

I’ve also been involved with the La Salle Computer Society and the DLSU Data Science Society, where collaboration, events and shared curiosity have stretched me beyond the technical side of my degree.

sections.label: HOW I WORK
sections.heading: Ask better questions.
sections.body:
I’m analytical and resourceful. Rather than accepting the first answer, I like to understand why something works, question assumptions, and try another approach when the result can be better.

When I’m away from a project, you’ll likely find me exploring a new tool, playing video or tabletop games, experimenting with design, or sketching out another app idea.

contact.label: WHAT’S NEXT
contact.heading: Let’s make something happen.
contact.body: I’m open to interesting projects, creative collaborations and opportunities to learn from different perspectives. Have something in mind?
